add_fruit.description: Propose a fruit for the public Fruityvice catalogue, which anyone may contribute to. Give the name, the family, genus and order, and the five nutrition figures per 100 grams. A Fruityvice admin reviews every proposal, so the fruit does not appear in any lookup until they approve it, and this step says so rather than reporting it as added. A fruit already in the catalogue is not sent again: the record that already exists comes back instead.

mock_response.message: Mangosteen was sent to Fruityvice and is waiting for an admin to review it. It will not appear in lookups until they approve it.
mock_response.name: Mangosteen

add_fruit.name: add_fruit

parameters.description: What the fruit is called. This is the name everyone reading Fruityvice will look it up by, so use the common English name on its own -- 'Mangosteen', not 'Fresh Mangosteen (Thailand)'. A fruit already in the catalogue is reported back with its existing record instead of being proposed again.

find_fruits.description: Every fruit Fruityvice holds, or only the ones that match. Narrow by botanical group (any family, genus or order, picked from a list that says which it is and how many fruits it reaches) and by a range on one of the five nutrition figures, together or apart. Sort by name or by any figure and cap the result, so 'the five lowest-sugar fruits' is one step. Leave every field empty for the whole catalogue.
find_fruits.name: find_fruits

parameters.description: Narrow to one botanical group. The list holds every family, genus and order in the catalogue, each labelled with which of the three it is and how many fruits it reaches, so 'Rutaceae - family, 5 fruits' can be picked without knowing what a family is. A few names are two kinds of group at once (Cactaceae is a family and a genus); they appear once and match both, and the result says which. Leave it empty for every fruit.

examples.label: The rose family, the largest here

parameters.name: group

parameters.description: Which figure to filter on. Fill in 'At least', 'At most' or both beside it: Fruityvice refuses a nutrition search with no range at all. Every figure is per 100 grams of fruit. Leave it empty to search without a nutrition filter.
parameters.name: nutrient

parameters.description: The lowest figure to include, counted in. Leave it empty for no lower limit. Only used when a nutrient is chosen.
parameters.name: min_value

parameters.description: The highest figure to include, counted in. Leave it empty for no upper limit. Only used when a nutrient is chosen.
parameters.name: max_value

parameters.description: What to order the results by. By name unless you say otherwise. Sorting by a figure is how to ask for the lowest-sugar or highest-protein fruits: order by it and set 'How many to return' to the number you want. A fruit with no figure for that nutrient comes last either way round, because 'not recorded' is not 'none'.
parameters.name: sort_by

parameters.description: Which way round to sort. Lowest first, or A to Z for names, unless you say otherwise.

parameters.description: How many fruits to return. Defaults to 50, which is more than the whole catalogue, so nothing is left out unless you ask for less. get_fruit.description: Look up one fruit and get its calories, fat, sugar, carbohydrate and protein per 100 grams, along with the botanical family, genus and order it belongs to. Ask by name in whatever capitalisation and spacing you have ('green apple' finds GreenApple) or by part of a name, or by catalogue number. All 49 fruits are findable by name here, including the four the service's own lookup cannot return. A name nothing matches comes back with the closest spellings rather than as a failed step.
get_fruit.name: get_fruit

parameters.description: Which fruit to look up. Pick it from the list, or hand one in from an earlier step: a name in any capitalisation, with or without the spaces Fruityvice does or does not use ('green apple' finds GreenApple, 'kiwi fruit' finds Kiwifruit), part of a name when only one fruit fits it, or the catalogue number. A name that fits several fruits comes back naming them rather than picking one, and a name that fits none comes back with the closest spellings.

description: Look up the nutrition and botany of 49 fruits: calories, fat, sugar, carbohydrate and protein per 100 grams, plus the family, genus and order each one belongs to. Get a single fruit by name, search the catalogue by botanical group and by a nutrition range at once, and propose a fruit of your own for the public catalogue. Fruityvice is free and keyless: no account, no API key, nothing to set up.
